packageRules.description: These packs exist to pin, so every update must be an exact version — never a range. Mirrors the npmOnlyValidator rule in build.gradle.kts, which fails the gate on a range.

@types/node must track the Node RUNTIME major (.nvmrc v22, node:22-alpine images), not npm latest. Typing against Node 26 APIs that do not exist at runtime is a bug, not an upgrade. Raise this ceiling only when the runtime moves.

Never propose engines bumps. engines.node/npm declare the RUNTIME floor these packs are built for (.nvmrc v22, node:22-alpine images) — the same reason @types/node is capped. Raising them here would claim support for a runtime nothing actually runs on. Move them by hand when the runtime moves.

Ceiling comes from @typescript-eslint's peer range (>=4.8.4 <6.1.0), not from the next major number. TS 7 restructured the compiler API and typescript-estree crashes on it (ts.Extension.Cjs undefined), failing lint for every consumer; 6.1+ is equally unsupported. Re-derive this ceiling from the peer range when typescript-eslint widens it.

Hold chai below 6 until consumers migrate. chai 6 is ESM-only with a changed assertion API and every module's test suite is written against 4.x — bumping it here would break the fleet in one release. @types/chai must match the chai major.
Internal ZeroBias packages can carry breaking contract changes — surface them on the dashboard and require a human to approve before a PR opens.
Toolchain patch/minor updates — grouped into one PR so the fleet moves in a single pack release.
Majors are a fleet-wide event: every consumer inherits them from one pack release. Keep them separate and never grouped.

prBodyNotes: ⚠️ **This pack is consumed by ~293 packages.** Merging publishes a new pack version, and every consumer picks it up on its next install. Check the changelog for behaviour changes before merging, and bump the pack version in this PR — the publish pipeline releases whatever version is on `main`.
